answer: Each challenge is cryptographically bound to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse whose value is unknown at task issuance and difficult to bias after quorum aggregation. A claimant must commit before the pulse and reveal a valid response afterward, so an automated sybil swarm cannot pre-compute solutions, recycle an echo, or farm challenges offline. The resulting ripple of unpredictable inputs ties each proof to a specific voyage through time and limits identity multiplication as a source of advantage.
